internet: Drops repeatedly, reconnects, then drops again.
Browsing, streaming or downloads are much slower than expected.
Connected to Wi-Fi but no internet
The device says it is connected, but websites/services do not load.
Wi-Fi works on other devices but not mine
Wi-Fi is weak in one room
Connection becomes unreliable farther from the router.
A newly connected phone/computer cannot join normally.
The network is visible but the password/connection fails.
The connection alternates between normal and unusable.
Something else is wrong with the connection.
device: Apps or normal actions take unusually long.
The screen or system stops responding normally.
It restarts or shuts down without you intentionally doing so.
Battery life is noticeably worse than your normal baseline.
The device reports low or nearly full storage.
It becomes warmer than expected during ordinary use.
One or several apps repeatedly close or freeze.
The issue appeared after a system/app update.
A built-in hardware feature behaves unexpectedly.
Something else is wrong with the device.
software: The app closes or freezes repeatedly.
Sign-in fails even though the account should work.
The app responds much more slowly than usual.
A specific button, screen or function fails.
Installation or updating does not complete normally.
A document, image, project or other file behaves unexpectedly.
Changes do not appear across devices/services.
Something else is wrong with software.
website: The page fails to open or keeps loading.
Pages or actions take unusually long.
Sign-in does not work as expected.
A submission, button, upload or action fails.
Images, layout, text or controls appear incorrect.
Website works on PC but not phone
The same site behaves differently by device.
Website works in one browser only
Something else is wrong with a website.
study: I keep delaying even when I know what to do.
I start but repeatedly switch tasks or get distracted.
I do not know what to study first
Too many tasks and no clear priority.
Work accumulates faster than I can complete it.
Good days are followed by long gaps.
I keep making the same mistakes
My test performance is lower than preparation
I study but performance does not match preparation.
I spend too much time on one topic
A chapter/question set takes much longer than planned.
household: Water/moisture is appearing where it normally should not.
An appliance/object is making an unusual noise
The sound is different from normal operation.
A household item is not working normally
Something needs ordinary user-level cleaning or care.
A door/drawer/cabinet is not behaving normally
It sticks, does not close, or behaves differently.
A visible household electrical symptom is present.
A new or unexpected odor is noticeable.
other: A device, process, object or service is failing.
An action takes much longer than expected.
A message or unexpected response appears.
The result changed from the normal behavior.
I do not know what is wrong
The symptom is unclear and needs structured diagnosis.
It works for someone else but not me
None of the listed problems fit.

symptoms: Pages/videos take too long to load.
Wi-Fi disconnects or stops working intermittently.
Connected to Wi-Fi but nothing loads.
Only one device has the problem
Connection is much worse farther from the router.

questions.q: Does the same problem happen on another device connected to the same Wi-Fi?
Does restarting the router temporarily improve it?
questions.yl: Yes — restart helps for a while

questions.q: Is the problem worse in one physical location?
Does it happen at roughly the same time of day?

multi.title: Likely network-side issue
multi.why: Multiple devices showing the same symptom points away from a single device.

steps.title: Observe
steps.action: Test two different devices for 2–3 minutes.
steps.detail: You should be able to tell whether the issue is shared.

steps.title: Restart
steps.action: Restart the router/modem using its normal power procedure.
steps.detail: Wait until its normal status lights/connection return.

steps.title: Compare
steps.action: Test again near the router and then at the original location.
steps.detail: A large difference suggests coverage/interference rather than the internet line itself.

steps.title: Record
steps.action: Write down the time, duration, affected devices and exact symptom.
steps.detail: This gives your ISP/support team useful evidence.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: If multiple devices still fail, contact the internet provider or responsible adult.
steps.detail: Provide the observations instead of only saying “Wi-Fi is bad.”

single.title: Likely device-side issue
single.why: If other devices work, investigate the affected device before changing the whole network.

steps.title: Reconnect
steps.action: Forget/reconnect to the Wi-Fi network using the device’s normal settings.
steps.detail: Confirm the device receives a normal connection.

steps.title: Restart
steps.action: Restart the affected device.
steps.detail: Retest before changing additional settings.

steps.title: Compare
steps.action: Test another network if one is safely available.
steps.detail: If the device works elsewhere, the original network/device interaction becomes more relevant.

steps.title: Update
steps.action: Check for normal system/network-driver updates.
steps.detail: Only install updates from the device’s normal trusted update channel.

steps.title: Record
steps.action: Capture the exact error or behavior if it remains.
steps.detail: Use the evidence when seeking support.

router.title: Temporary recovery after router restart
router.why: A temporary improvement suggests the network equipment or connection may be involved, but it does not prove the cause.

steps.title: Observe
steps.action: Note how long the connection remains stable after recovery.
steps.detail: A repeatable pattern is useful evidence.

steps.title: Compare
steps.action: Check whether all connected devices are affected when it happens again.
steps.detail: This separates shared from device-specific symptoms.

steps.title: Position
steps.action: If the issue is location-dependent, compare near and far from the router.
steps.detail: Large differences point toward coverage.

steps.title: Record
steps.action: Record timestamps and symptoms for two or three occurrences.
steps.detail: Patterns are more useful than a single incident.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: If the problem repeatedly returns, involve the ISP or responsible adult.
steps.detail: Share the pattern and affected devices.

signal.title: Likely coverage/interference issue
signal.why: A location-dependent symptom makes the physical Wi-Fi path important.

steps.title: Compare
steps.action: Test near the router and in the problem location.
steps.detail: Measure the practical difference by loading the same simple page.

steps.title: Reduce distance
steps.action: For important work, temporarily use a location with a stronger signal.
steps.detail: This is a workaround, not proof of the root cause.

steps.title: Check pattern
steps.action: See whether walls, floors or one specific room consistently correlate with the problem.
steps.detail: A repeatable location pattern is useful evidence.

steps.title: Record
steps.action: Write down the locations where the connection is reliable/unreliable.
steps.detail: Use this before considering network changes.

timing.title: Time-pattern investigation
timing.why: A repeated time pattern can point to congestion, scheduled activity, or an external event.

steps.title: Log
steps.action: Record start/end times for several occurrences.
steps.detail: Look for a repeated window rather than one coincidence.

steps.title: Compare
steps.action: Check whether every device is affected during that window.
steps.detail: Shared timing strengthens the network-side hypothesis.

steps.title: Cross-check
steps.action: Compare with another network or ask whether the same service is affected elsewhere.
steps.detail: This helps separate local from service-wide problems.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: If the pattern persists, provide the timestamps to the responsible support team.
steps.detail: Precise timestamps are actionable evidence.

persistent.title: Persistent connection issue
persistent.why: Because a restart does not resolve the issue, focus on reproducible evidence rather than repeatedly restarting.

steps.title: Reproduce
steps.action: Trigger the problem once and note the exact symptom.
steps.detail: Avoid changing several settings at once.

steps.title: Compare
steps.action: Test another device on the same network.
steps.detail: This is the key split between network and device diagnosis.

steps.title: Compare location
steps.action: Test near the router if relevant.
steps.detail: A location change can reveal a coverage component.

steps.title: Record
steps.action: Keep a short incident log with time, device and symptom.
steps.detail: Use it for support.

not-signal.title: General network diagnosis
not-signal.why: No obvious location pattern means you need to separate device, router and service symptoms systematically.

steps.title: Compare devices
steps.action: Test at least two devices.
steps.detail: Determine whether the symptom is shared.

steps.title: Restart once
steps.action: Restart the relevant device/network equipment through normal controls.
steps.detail: Then retest.

steps.title: Observe
steps.action: Record exactly what fails: connection, DNS/page loading, speed, or one service.
steps.detail: Specific symptoms narrow the next step.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: If multiple devices fail repeatedly, involve the ISP/support team.
steps.detail: Give them your observations.

not-timing.title: Repeatable network diagnosis
not-timing.why: Without a time pattern, device/location comparison gives the most useful information.

steps.title: Compare devices
steps.action: Test another device on the same network.
steps.detail: Shared vs single-device behavior is the first split.

steps.title: Compare location
steps.action: Test near and far from the router.
steps.detail: This checks coverage.

steps.title: Record
steps.action: Write the exact symptom and when it occurs.
steps.detail: Keep the evidence consistent.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: Use the collected evidence if the issue remains.
steps.detail: Avoid random setting changes.

evidence: What changed immediately before it started

symptoms: Apps open slowly or actions lag.
One or more apps close, freeze or become unresponsive.
Battery falls faster than your normal baseline.
The device restarts without you intentionally doing it.

questions.q: Does the problem affect one app or many parts of the device?
Did the problem start after an update, install, or setting change?
Does a normal restart temporarily improve it?
questions.yl: Yes — restart helps for a while

single.title: App-specific device issue
single.why: A problem isolated to one app should be investigated at the app level first.

steps.title: Reproduce
steps.action: Open the app and trigger the problem once.
steps.detail: Record the exact behavior.

steps.title: Restart app
steps.action: Close and reopen the app normally.
steps.detail: Retest before changing settings.

steps.title: Update
steps.action: Check the app’s official update channel.
steps.detail: Install an update only if one is offered there.

steps.title: Compare
steps.action: If possible, check whether the same account/service works elsewhere.
steps.detail: This helps separate app from account/service issues.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: If the issue persists, record the app version and exact error.
steps.detail: Use official support.

broad.title: System-wide device issue
broad.why: Multiple affected areas make a system-level cause more relevant than one app.

steps.title: Check storage
steps.action: Look at the device’s storage status.
steps.detail: Very low free space can affect normal operation.

steps.title: Restart
steps.action: Perform one normal restart.
steps.detail: Retest the same actions afterward.

steps.title: Update
steps.action: Check normal system updates.
steps.detail: Use only the device’s built-in update path.

steps.title: Observe
steps.action: Note whether the problem appears during a particular activity or after a particular action.
steps.detail: Patterns help distinguish causes.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: If unexpected restarts or persistent system failures continue, involve a trusted adult or qualified service provider.
steps.detail: Bring the observations rather than repeatedly experimenting.

change.title: Recent-change investigation
change.why: A new update, installation or setting change creates a strong timeline clue.

steps.title: Identify
steps.action: Write down what changed immediately before the problem began.
steps.detail: Be specific: app, update, setting or accessory.

steps.title: Test safely
steps.action: Use normal app/device settings to return only the recent change if there is an obvious reversible option.
steps.detail: Do not modify advanced system settings blindly.

steps.title: Retest
steps.action: Repeat the original action.
steps.detail: Check whether the symptom changes.

steps.title: Record
steps.action: Keep the before/after observation.
steps.detail: This is stronger evidence than memory.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: If the issue remains or the device behaves unpredictably, use official support/service.
steps.detail: Avoid risky hardware modifications.

nochange.title: Baseline comparison
nochange.why: Without a known recent change, compare scope, reproduction and system state.

steps.title: Define
steps.action: Write the exact symptom and one reproducible example.
steps.detail: Avoid vague descriptions such as “it is broken.”

steps.title: Scope
steps.action: Check whether one app, one feature, or the whole device is affected.
steps.detail: This determines the next branch.

steps.title: Check basics
steps.action: Review storage and normal updates.
steps.detail: Do not change advanced settings yet.

steps.title: Restart
steps.action: Restart once and compare.
steps.detail: Record whether anything changed.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: If persistent, use official support/service with your evidence.
steps.detail: Bring your notes, the device model and the exact symptom to the manufacturer, your carrier or a qualified repair shop.

restart.title: Temporary recovery after restart
restart.why: Temporary improvement suggests state, resource, or software interaction issues but does not identify the root cause.

steps.title: Observe
steps.action: Note how long the device works normally after restart.
steps.detail: Repeat only enough to establish a pattern.

steps.title: Scope
steps.action: Identify the exact app/action that eventually triggers the issue.
steps.detail: This narrows the investigation.

steps.title: Check basics
steps.action: Review storage and available updates.
steps.detail: Use built-in settings.

steps.title: Record
steps.action: Keep a short incident log.
steps.detail: Time + action + symptom is enough.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: If repeated restarts become necessary, seek official support.
steps.detail: If restarts keep being needed, or the device shuts down by itself, stop experimenting and contact official support.

persistent.title: Persistent device issue
persistent.why: Because restarting does not help, focus on scope and evidence instead of repeating the same action.

steps.title: Define
steps.action: Record one exact reproducible symptom.
steps.detail: Write one sentence: what you do, what you expect, and what actually happens. One clear example beats a general complaint.

steps.title: Scope
steps.action: Check whether it is one app or system-wide.
steps.detail: Try the same action in another app or feature. The same result everywhere suggests a system-wide issue; only one place suggests an app issue.

steps.title: Check basics
steps.action: Review storage and normal updates.
steps.detail: Open Settings and note your free storage and whether an update is waiting.

steps.title: Avoid random changes
steps.action: Do not alter advanced settings without knowing what they do.
steps.detail: Changing unknown settings can create new problems and hide the original one. Change one thing at a time, and only if you can undo it.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: Use official support/service if the problem remains.
steps.detail: Contact the manufacturer or a trusted repair service with your notes, model and OS version.

symptoms: Actions take much longer than expected.
A file is missing, wrong, or cannot be opened.
Sign-in or account behavior is failing.

questions.q: Can you reproduce the issue consistently?
Is there a specific error message or code?
Did an update, install, setting, or file change happen first?
Does the same problem happen with a different file, account, or project?

repeat.title: Reproducible software issue
repeat.why: A repeatable failure is easier to diagnose because each test can be compared.

steps.title: Reproduce once
steps.action: Trigger the issue and capture the exact message/behavior.
steps.detail: Do not repeatedly retry if it risks changing data.

steps.title: Isolate
steps.action: Change only one safe variable at a time.
steps.detail: For example, test another file or account if appropriate.

steps.title: Check version
steps.action: Record the software version and platform.
steps.detail: Use the official about/help screen.

steps.title: Check official support
steps.action: Search the exact error in the software maker’s official support documentation.
steps.detail: Prefer official documentation over random fixes.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: If unresolved, provide the reproduction steps and evidence to support.
steps.detail: Send support the steps that trigger it, the exact error, the app version and your platform.

intermittent.title: Intermittent software issue
intermittent.why: Intermittent failures require logging because memory after the fact is unreliable.

steps.title: Start a log
steps.action: Record date/time, action, file/account and symptom.
steps.detail: A note on your phone is enough: date, time, what you were doing and what happened.

steps.title: Look for triggers
steps.action: After several incidents, compare what was common.
steps.detail: Do not assume the first coincidence is causal.

steps.title: Update safely
steps.action: Check the official update channel.
steps.detail: Use only the app store or the software's own update option, never third-party download sites.

steps.title: Reduce variables
steps.action: When possible, reproduce with a simple known-good input.
steps.detail: Try a small, simple file or a fresh test account so fewer things can go wrong at once.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: Share the incident pattern with support.
steps.detail: Give support your log and what the incidents had in common.

error.title: Error-led diagnosis
error.why: An exact error code is often more informative than a general description.

steps.title: Copy exactly
steps.action: Record the error text/code without paraphrasing.
steps.detail: Copy the message or take a screenshot. Codes and exact wording are what support searches for.

steps.title: Capture context
steps.action: Write what action caused it and what you expected.
steps.detail: Note what you clicked just before it appeared and what you expected to happen.

steps.title: Check official docs
steps.action: Search the exact error in the software maker’s official help/support.
steps.detail: Search the exact text on the maker's own help site. Ignore answers that tell you to disable security features.

steps.title: Test one documented fix
steps.action: Apply one relevant, low-risk documented action.
steps.detail: Pick one low-risk fix from the official page. Doing several at once means you won't know which one worked.

steps.title: Record result
steps.action: Note whether the error changed, disappeared, or stayed identical.
steps.detail: Did the error disappear, change or stay identical? A changed error is progress, so record the new text.

noerror.title: Behavior-led diagnosis
noerror.why: Without an error, scope and reproduction become the strongest clues.

steps.title: Define
steps.action: Describe the expected vs actual behavior.
steps.detail: Write "I expected X, but Y happened". That gap is what support needs.

steps.title: Reproduce
steps.action: Find the smallest sequence that reliably triggers it.
steps.detail: Find the shortest set of clicks that triggers it every time.

steps.title: Compare
steps.action: Try a known-good file/action if possible.
steps.detail: Try another file, account or project. If it works there, the problem is tied to the original item.

steps.title: Check updates
steps.action: Use the official update channel.
steps.detail: Update using the official update option, then retest the same sequence.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: Share exact reproduction steps if the issue persists.
steps.detail: Share your exact steps, the expected vs actual result, and the version.

recent.title: Recent-change investigation
recent.why: A timeline gives you a concrete hypothesis without guessing.

steps.title: Identify
steps.action: Record the exact change and timestamp if known.
steps.detail: Note the exact update, install or setting, and roughly when it happened.

steps.title: Compare
steps.action: Check whether the issue existed before the change.
steps.detail: Ask yourself whether it worked the day before. If it did, the change is a strong suspect.

steps.title: Use documented rollback
steps.action: If the software officially provides a safe undo/restore path, follow that documentation.
steps.detail: Do not delete or overwrite important data blindly.

steps.title: Retest
steps.action: Repeat the original action.
steps.detail: Repeat exactly the action that failed and compare with before.

steps.title: Record
steps.action: Keep the before/after result.
steps.detail: Write down what changed and what didn't. This gives support a clear timeline.

norecent.title: Baseline software diagnosis
norecent.why: Without a recent change, establish a reproducible baseline first.

steps.title: Define
steps.action: Write expected vs actual behavior.
steps.detail: Write the symptom plus one example you can repeat.

steps.title: Reproduce
steps.action: Find a minimal reproducible example.
steps.detail: Find a repeatable trigger. If it happens randomly, start a log instead.

steps.title: Check version
steps.action: Record software/platform version.
steps.detail: Find it under About or Help. Support will ask for it first.

steps.title: Check official support
steps.action: Look for known issues/documentation.
steps.detail: Search your exact symptom on the software maker's site.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: Provide the reproduction steps and evidence.
steps.detail: Send the version, platform, steps and evidence to official support.

symptoms: The page fails to load at all.
Layout, buttons, images or content are broken.
Sign-in does not work as expected.
Pages or actions take unusually long.
A button, upload, or form submission does not work.

questions.q: Does the problem go away when you use a different browser?
Does it happen on another device or network?
Is there a visible error message?

browser.title: Browser-specific investigation
browser.why: If another browser works, the original browser becomes the first variable to isolate.

steps.title: Compare
steps.action: Repeat the same action in the working and failing browser.
steps.detail: Keep the test identical.

steps.title: Private test
steps.action: Try a private/incognito window in the failing browser.
steps.detail: This can separate session/extension effects.

steps.title: Check extensions
steps.action: If private mode works, review browser extensions one at a time.
steps.detail: Disable only what you understand.

steps.title: Clear only if appropriate
steps.action: Use the browser’s normal site-data controls if official support recommends it.
steps.detail: Avoid deleting important saved information blindly.

steps.title: Record
steps.action: Keep the exact browser/version and error.
steps.detail: Use this when reporting the issue.

broad.title: Cross-device/service investigation
broad.why: If multiple devices or networks reproduce it, a local browser issue becomes less likely.

steps.title: Confirm
steps.action: Repeat the same action on a second device/network.
steps.detail: Try the same site on another device and network (for example mobile data). If it fails everywhere, the problem is probably the site.

steps.title: Record
steps.action: Capture exact error, URL/page and time.
steps.detail: Note the time, the page and any message. Screenshots help.

steps.title: Check official status/support
steps.action: If the website provides an official status page or support channel, check it.
steps.detail: Look for a status page or the company's official account for outage notices.

steps.title: Wait-and-retest
steps.action: For service-side issues, retest later rather than repeatedly changing local settings.
steps.detail: Wait 15 to 30 minutes and test again. Don't keep retrying anything that involves payments or submitting forms.

steps.title: Report
steps.action: Send the exact reproduction steps to the website owner/support.
steps.detail: Contact the site's support with the time, page, error and what you tried.

local.title: Local browser/session investigation
local.why: If another environment works, focus on the original device/browser/session.

steps.title: Refresh
steps.action: Reload once and repeat the action.
steps.detail: Do a hard refresh (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+R) or close and reopen the tab.

steps.title: Private test
steps.action: Try a private/incognito window.
steps.detail: Open the page in a private/incognito window. If it works there, extensions or cached data may be involved.

steps.title: Browser comparison
steps.action: Try another supported browser.
steps.detail: Try a second browser. If it works there, the first browser is the likely cause.

steps.title: Check session
steps.action: If appropriate, sign out/in through the site’s normal controls.
steps.detail: Sign out and back in. Expired sessions cause many odd failures.

steps.title: Record
steps.action: Document what works and what fails.
steps.detail: Note which browser and mode worked and which didn't.

notbrowser.title: Browser-neutral web diagnosis
notbrowser.why: Because another browser does not reproduce the issue, investigate whether the problem is local or service-side.

steps.title: Compare device
steps.action: Test another device if safely available.
steps.detail: Try another phone or computer on the same network.

steps.title: Compare network
steps.action: Test another network if safely available.
steps.detail: Switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data to see whether your network is blocking or slowing the site.

steps.title: Record error
steps.action: Capture exact text and page.
steps.detail: Copy the exact message shown, and the time.

steps.title: Check official support
steps.action: Use the website’s official support/status information.
steps.detail: Check the site's help pages for that message.

steps.title: Report
steps.action: Provide concise reproduction steps.
steps.detail: Send support your device, browser, network type and the error.

error.title: Error-led web diagnosis
error.why: The exact error is the strongest evidence available at this stage.

steps.title: Capture
steps.action: Copy the exact error text/code and page.
steps.detail: Screenshot the message including the address bar. Don't retype it from memory.

steps.title: Reproduce
steps.action: Confirm the same action produces it.
steps.detail: Repeat the same steps once to see whether the error is consistent.

steps.title: Compare
steps.action: Test another browser/device if possible.
steps.detail: Try another browser or device to see whether the error follows you.

steps.title: Check official support
steps.action: Search the exact error using the site’s official support information.
steps.detail: Search the exact message on the site's official help centre.

steps.title: Report
steps.action: Include URL/page, time, browser/device and error.
steps.detail: Send the screenshot, time and what you tried to the site's support.

noerror.title: Behavior-led web diagnosis
noerror.why: Without an error, cross-environment comparison is the fastest way to narrow the scope.

steps.title: Define
steps.action: Write expected vs actual behavior.
steps.detail: Write what should happen and what actually happens.

steps.title: Compare browser
steps.action: Try another supported browser.
steps.detail: Test in a second browser. Different results point to the browser.

steps.title: Compare device/network
steps.action: Try another environment if available.
steps.detail: Try another device or network to rule out your setup.

steps.title: Record
steps.action: Note what combination works/fails.
steps.detail: Note the browser, device, network and which combinations worked.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: Report the smallest reproducible sequence.
steps.detail: Give the site's support your comparison notes; it saves them time.

symptoms: I know I should study but keep delaying.
I start but repeatedly switch tasks.
I study but cannot recall later.
I do not know what to study
I have too much work and no clear priority.
Some days go well, then the routine collapses.

questions.q: Do you have one clearly defined task for the next session?
Is the main interruption coming from your environment/device?
Can you explain what you studied without looking at your notes?
questions.yl: Yes — I can explain most of it

clear.title: Execution problem
clear.why: When the next task is clear, the main bottleneck is usually starting and protecting attention.

steps.title: Shrink
steps.action: Define a 15–30 minute unit of work.
steps.detail: Make the finish line visible.

steps.title: Remove one distraction
steps.action: Put the biggest avoidable interruption out of reach.
steps.detail: Change the environment before starting.

steps.title: Start timer
steps.action: Work only on the defined task for one short block.
steps.detail: Do not optimize the system mid-session.

steps.title: Record friction
steps.action: After the block, write what interrupted you.
steps.detail: One sentence is enough.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.action: Use the friction note to change the next session.
steps.detail: Build from evidence rather than motivation.

unclear.title: Planning bottleneck
unclear.why: If the next task is unclear, motivation is not the first problem — task selection is.

steps.title: List
steps.action: Write every pending task without organizing it yet.
steps.detail: Write every task down, even small ones. Seeing the whole list removes the strain of holding it in your head.

steps.title: Define
steps.action: For each important task, write the smallest next action.
steps.detail: Example: “solve Q1–5” instead of “study physics.”

steps.title: Prioritize
steps.action: Choose one urgent/high-value next action.
steps.detail: Only one starting task.

steps.title: Time-box
steps.action: Give it a short block.
steps.detail: Give the first task a fixed short block (say 25 minutes) and stop when it ends, even if unfinished.

steps.title: Review
steps.action: At the end, choose the next action before stopping.
steps.detail: This reduces tomorrow’s startup friction.

distraction.title: Environment bottleneck
distraction.why: If the main interruption is external, changing the environment can have more leverage than trying to force concentration.

steps.title: Identify
steps.action: Name the top one distraction.
steps.detail: For one session, note each time you get pulled away and what pulled you.

steps.title: Remove
steps.action: Change one environmental variable before starting.
steps.detail: Put your phone in another room and close unrelated tabs before you begin.

steps.title: Focus block
steps.action: Work for a short defined block.
steps.detail: Work in one timed block on one task, then take a real break.

steps.title: Log interruptions
steps.action: Record what still broke focus.
steps.detail: Keep a tally of interruptions. If it drops, the change is working.

steps.title: Iterate
steps.action: Change only the biggest remaining interruption next time.
steps.detail: After a few days, keep what reduced distractions and drop what didn't.

internal.title: Attention/energy investigation
internal.why: When external distractions are not dominant, task size, difficulty and timing are worth testing.

steps.title: Check task size
steps.action: Reduce the task to a concrete 15–30 minute unit.
steps.detail: If a task feels heavy, cut it into a piece you can finish in about 20 minutes.

steps.title: Change timing
steps.action: Compare a different time of day on the next session.
steps.detail: Try studying at a different time of day. Your energy may be better then.

steps.title: Use active work
steps.action: For learning, alternate input with recall/practice.
steps.detail: Swap re-reading for solving questions, explaining aloud or writing from memory.

steps.title: Record difficulty
steps.action: Note where you got stuck instead of simply stopping.
steps.detail: Note where you get stuck or bored. That is the real problem to solve.

steps.title: Adjust
steps.action: Use the pattern to choose the next session format.
steps.detail: Change one thing (task size, time or method) and review after a few days.

recall.title: Retention is the next lever
recall.why: Being able to retrieve information without notes is a stronger test of learning than rereading alone.

steps.title: Close notes
steps.action: After a study block, put notes away.
steps.detail: Shut your notes and write everything you remember on a blank page.

steps.title: Recall
steps.action: Write or say the key ideas from memory.
steps.detail: Pull the topic out of memory without looking. The effort is what strengthens it.

steps.title: Check
steps.action: Compare your recall with the source.
steps.detail: Compare your page to the notes and mark what was missing or wrong.

steps.title: Log gaps
steps.action: Record exactly what you could not recall.
steps.detail: Keep a running list of gaps so your next session starts there.

steps.title: Re-test
steps.action: Return to those gaps later using retrieval/practice.
steps.detail: Test yourself again after a day or two, and again after a week.

weakrecall.title: Active-recall diagnosis
weakrecall.why: If you cannot retrieve the material without notes, the next action should test and strengthen retrieval.

steps.title: Close notes
steps.action: Attempt recall before rereading.
steps.detail: Put your notes away before you test yourself.

steps.title: Generate questions
steps.action: Turn the material into a few questions.
steps.detail: Write 5 to 10 questions about the topic that you might be asked on a test.

steps.title: Answer
steps.action: Answer without looking.
steps.detail: Answer them from memory, then check.

steps.title: Check gaps
steps.action: Mark only the missed concepts.
steps.detail: Mark the ones you got wrong or answered slowly. These are your real weak spots.

steps.title: Re-test later
steps.action: Space the next retrieval attempt instead of immediately rereading everything.
steps.detail: Come back to the same questions after a few days to see whether they stuck.

symptoms: A loose, blocked, leaking, noisy, or misaligned non-hazardous item.
The item needs routine cleaning or care.
The behavior changed during normal use.

questions.q: Could this involve electricity, gas, fire, chemicals, pressure, sharp machinery, or structural damage?
questions.nl: No — none that I can see

questions.q: Can you inspect the issue without opening, dismantling, cutting, lifting, or touching a hazardous component?
questions.nl: No — would need to open or touch it

questions.q: Do you have the manual or the manufacturer instructions for this item?

hazard.title: Safety stop
hazard.why: Some household problems can become dangerous when a person experiments with them.

steps.title: Stop
steps.action: Do not continue troubleshooting the hazardous component.
steps.detail: Do not touch, open or repair the item. Stepping away is the right move.

steps.title: Secure
steps.action: Move away from the suspected hazard and follow normal emergency/safety procedures if there is immediate danger.
steps.detail: Keep people and pets away. Switch the item off with its normal control only if that is clearly safe. Never touch anything wet, hot or sparking.

steps.title: Tell an adult
steps.action: Inform a trusted adult about the exact visible symptom.
steps.detail: Tell a parent, guardian or the person responsible for the home right away.

steps.title: Professional help
steps.action: Use a qualified professional for inspection/repair when appropriate.
steps.detail: Call a licensed electrician, plumber or gas engineer. For fire, a gas smell or serious danger, call your local emergency number.

steps.title: Record safely
steps.action: Only note visible, non-hazardous symptoms if it is safe to do so.
steps.detail: Take a photo from a safe distance and note the time and what you saw. Don't move closer for a better picture.

stop.title: Do not dismantle
stop.why: If safe observation is not possible, the correct diagnostic action is escalation rather than experimentation.

steps.title: Stop
steps.action: Do not open or dismantle the item.
steps.detail: If you can't check it without opening or touching something hazardous, don't continue.

steps.title: Tell an adult
steps.action: Describe what happened and what you observed.
steps.detail: Explain to them what you saw and why you stopped.

steps.title: Professional help
steps.action: Ask a qualified person to inspect it.
steps.detail: A qualified person should handle anything you can't inspect safely.

steps.title: Record
steps.action: Keep the model/name and visible symptom if safe.
steps.detail: Note what you observed and when, from a safe distance.

visible.title: Safe visible-check workflow
visible.why: Only routine, non-hazardous observations are appropriate here.

steps.title: Observe
steps.action: Describe exactly what looks or behaves differently.
steps.detail: Look closely at the outside only. Note loose parts, blockages, marks or damage.

steps.title: Check normal controls
steps.action: Use only the normal user controls/instructions for the item.
steps.detail: Check plug and switch position, batteries, settings and the on/off state you'd normally use.

steps.title: Clean if documented
steps.action: If routine cleaning is explicitly described by the manufacturer, follow that documentation.
steps.detail: Clean only in the ways the manual describes, with the item off and cool.

steps.title: Retest
steps.action: Use the item normally and compare.
steps.detail: Try the item again normally and compare with before.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: If the issue remains or becomes unsafe, stop and involve an adult/professional.
steps.detail: If nothing changed, check the manual or contact the maker or a professional.

safe.title: Safety-first household diagnosis
safe.why: Before any action, rule out hazards and keep the investigation limited to normal user-level checks.

steps.title: Describe
steps.action: Record the visible symptom.
steps.detail: Write what's wrong, when it began and what normally happens.

steps.title: Check instructions
steps.action: Use the manufacturer’s normal user guidance if available.
steps.detail: Find the manual or manufacturer's page and see whether your symptom is listed.

steps.title: Try one safe action
steps.action: Change one normal-use variable at a time.
steps.detail: Pick one simple, documented action. Nothing that involves opening or dismantling.

steps.title: Retest
steps.action: Compare with the original symptom.
steps.detail: Check whether the symptom changed.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: Stop if anything becomes hazardous or unclear.
steps.detail: If nothing changes, ask a trusted adult, the maker or a professional.

symptoms: A device, process, object, or service is failing.
You did something normal and got an unexpected outcome.
The same issue returns after temporary recovery.

questions.q: Can you reproduce the problem?
Did something change before it started?
Can you safely compare with a known-good example?
questions.yl: Yes — I have a working example

repeat.title: Reproducible problem
repeat.why: Repeatability lets you test one variable at a time.

steps.title: Define
steps.action: Write expected vs actual result.
steps.detail: Describe the problem in one sentence: what you did and what happened.

steps.title: Reproduce
steps.action: Find the smallest sequence that causes the issue.
steps.detail: Find the smallest sequence of actions that causes it each time.

steps.title: Change one thing
steps.action: Make one safe, reversible change.
steps.detail: Change only one thing, so you know what made the difference.

steps.title: Retest
steps.action: Compare with the original behavior.
steps.detail: Do exactly the same action again and compare.

steps.title: Document
steps.action: Keep the successful/failed test results.
steps.detail: Write down what you tried and what happened so you don't repeat it.

intermittent.title: Intermittent problem
intermittent.why: A log turns an unpredictable issue into a pattern you can investigate.

steps.title: Log
steps.action: Record time, context, action and symptom every time.
steps.detail: Note the date, time and what was happening each time.

steps.title: Compare
steps.action: After several incidents, look for repeated conditions.
steps.detail: Look at your log: what do the incidents have in common?

steps.title: Test one hypothesis
steps.action: Change one safe variable.
steps.detail: Pick one likely cause and test only that.

steps.title: Record result
steps.action: Write what changed.
steps.detail: Write down whether the test changed anything.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: Use the evidence if specialist help is needed.
steps.detail: Share your log with whoever supports this.

change.title: Recent-change investigation
change.why: A clear timeline gives you a testable hypothesis.

steps.title: Identify
steps.action: Write what changed immediately before the issue.
steps.detail: Think back to what changed before it began: a setting, a place, a person, a product?

steps.title: Compare
steps.action: Check whether the issue existed before that change.
steps.detail: Compare how it worked before with how it works now.

steps.title: Undo safely
steps.action: If there is an obvious normal-user undo path, use it.
steps.detail: Reverse the change only if it can be undone easily and safely.

steps.title: Retest
steps.action: Repeat the original action.
steps.detail: Repeat the original action and compare.

steps.title: Document
steps.action: Keep the before/after evidence.
steps.detail: Note what changed and whether undoing it helped.

nochange.title: Baseline investigation
nochange.why: Without a known change, scope and reproduction are the best starting points.

steps.title: Define
steps.action: Write the exact symptom.
steps.detail: State the problem and give one real example.

steps.title: Reproduce
steps.action: Find a repeatable example if possible.
steps.detail: Find a repeatable trigger.

steps.title: Compare
steps.action: Use a known-good example if safely available.
steps.detail: Compare with a working example if you can find one.

steps.title: Change one variable
steps.action: Test one safe possibility.
steps.detail: Change one variable, retest and write down the result.

steps.title: Document
steps.action: Keep what worked and what did not.
steps.detail: Keep notes so anyone helping you can see your tests.

compare.title: Known-good comparison
compare.why: A controlled comparison can reveal which variable differs.

steps.title: List variables
steps.action: Write what differs between working and failing cases.
steps.detail: List the differences between the working and non-working case: settings, place, version, timing, person.

steps.title: Choose one
steps.action: Pick one safe variable to test.
steps.detail: Choose the difference you suspect most.

steps.title: Retest
steps.action: Make only that change.
steps.detail: Make the two match on that one point and test again.

steps.title: Record
steps.action: Note whether the symptom changes.
steps.detail: Write down what happened.

steps.title: Repeat carefully
steps.action: Test the next variable only if needed.
steps.detail: Repeat with the next difference, changing only one thing each time.

nocompare.title: Evidence-first diagnosis
nocompare.why: Without a known-good comparison, build a reliable description before changing things.

steps.title: Define
steps.action: Write expected vs actual.
steps.detail: Say what you expected and what you got.

steps.title: Reproduce
steps.action: Try to create the symptom again.
steps.detail: Find a way to trigger it deliberately.

steps.title: Log
steps.action: Record time, context and exact behavior.
steps.detail: Log the time and conditions each time it happens.

steps.title: Change one safe variable
steps.action: Test only one hypothesis.
steps.detail: Change one safe thing and test.

steps.title: Escalate
steps.action: Use the evidence when asking for help.
steps.detail: Share your log and tests with the person or service that can help.
